title: Dark patterns in design, with examples from AI and blockchains

title: PICO Scholar: Advancing Open Research with an Open-Source AI Platform

description.en: Co-presented with Matias Vizcaino: an open-source AI platform to make systematic literature reviews faster, more accurate and open to all.
description.fr: Co-présenté avec Matias Vizcaino : une plateforme d'IA open source pour rendre les revues systématiques de littérature plus rapides, plus précises et ouvertes à tous.

abstract: PICO Scholar is an open-source project at the proof-of-concept stage, developed by a team from Georgia Tech's Master in Computer Science program with early guidance from Robert Gordon University. Recently recognized with a 2nd place finish at the Red Hat & Intel AI Hackathon, PICO Scholar aims to tackle the growing challenge of sifting through massive, fast-evolving literature, whether in healthcare, engineering, or education. Traditional search tools often struggle with specialized terminology, inconsistent metadata, and a lack of transparent workflows. By integrating domain-adaptive AI and real-time collaboration features, the platform offers a more robust, efficient way for researchers to discover, analyze, and evaluate relevant studies.

title: Technology challenges for privacy: the case of decentralised social media

description.en: The advantages and challenges of decentralised social media, seen through data protection law and privacy architectural strategies.
description.fr: Les atouts et les défis des réseaux sociaux décentralisés, vus à travers le prisme de la protection des données et des stratégies d'architecture de la vie privée.

abstract: As decentralized social media gathers more users, the privacy by design and default principles from the GDPR are in accordance with the design model it proposes. This talk tackles the main advantages and challenges this approach brings, from the perspective of data protection legislation and privacy architectural strategies, including data separation as a core strategy, and blockchain- and ActivityPub-based networks as the leading examples.

title: Open source in the quest for GDPR compliance

description.en: How the GDPR's principles connect to the open-source ecosystem, and how rights and responsibilities are shared between communities and their infrastructure providers.
description.fr: Comment les principes du RGPD se connectent à l'écosystème open source, et comment droits et responsabilités se répartissent entre les communautés et leurs hébergeurs d'infrastructure.

abstract: The OSS field has as core value the concept of community. Not surprisingly, a lot of OSS projects revolve around privacy, anonymity and data protection. This talk analyses how the provisions of the GDPR are tangential to the OSS ecosystem: how its principles connect to the OSS world, how the data controller / data processor model maps to OSS participants and infrastructure providers, and how data-protection rights are enforced by the OSS model, through technologies such as wikis and zero-knowledge collaborative software.

description.fr: Là où le droit à l'oubli rencontre le machine learning, et pourquoi la suppression est plus difficile qu'il n'y paraît.

title: Artificial intelligence dealing with the right to be forgotten

description.en: Human memory forgets; machine learning doesn't. What the right to be forgotten can even mean for AI systems, de lege lata and de lege ferenda.
description.fr: La mémoire humaine oublie ; le machine learning, non. Ce que le droit à l'oubli peut bien signifier pour les systèmes d'IA, de lege lata et de lege ferenda.

abstract: The right to be forgotten encounters difficulties in defining its applicability in the context of continuous tech evolution. AI development particularly raises problems due to the nature of machine learning and the differences between the memory processes of humans and AI systems. This talk analyses the right to be forgotten as a concept and its juridical nature, compares psychological memory with how AI systems 'remember', asks when deletion can be considered an act of forgetting, and explores potential legal and policy adaptations to current statutory law.
